text.p: These are the leading stories in the Maltese press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

THE TIMES - Growing shortage of doctors in public service. Dr Anthony Galea Debono, president of the Medical Association of Malta, is calling for urgent measures to stop a growing exodus of doctors from the public sector.
- Trade gap widens 5.5 percent in first three quarters.
- House of Representatives refurbished. The Parliament chamber has been given a much needed refurbishment, ahead of the planned opening of parliament next month.

L-ORIZZONT - British market remains the most important for tourism, minister says. Minister of Tourism Karmenu Vella met a delegation of tour operators and told them the British market remained the most important, even though it has declined to 46 percent of the total.

IN-NAZZJON - Nationalist Party to set up own television station, opposition leader Eddie Fenech Adami says. The Labour Party was the only one to have a TV station before the October 26 elections, and that has been seen as a factor which contributed to its electoral success.
